slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The Data Landscapers review states that national DHIS2 is used for aggregate reporting from district level, with paper registers at clinics transcribed upward; the document gives no date for this, so its publication date is used.

The Data Landscapers review states that pilots exist, citing some direct DHIS2 entry in one clinic, and that there is no evidence of majority point-of-service digital use in rural clinics; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Data Landscapers review states that rural primary healthcare clinics in Benin predominantly record patient data on paper registers and scores them as entirely paper-based; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Data Landscapers review states that Enabel equipped 244 facilities (rural or not unspecified) with IT for data collection but not point-of-care patient records, and scores rural clinics as entirely paper-based; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

systems.tiers: aggregate reporting from district level; direct entry in one clinic as a pilot
pilot, described only as for management

note: The document's own header marks its country figures as an AI-assisted compilation, the author's analysis rather than sourced fact. It also mentions a national eHealth strategy of 2017 aiming for a digital HIS, and 4,000 paper health data registers distributed to private facilities by Abt Global's PSHPA project.
